grants.purpose: Disable core dumps and ptrace, drop capabilities in Linux user namespace, and apply seccomp filter
grants.admits: Linux unshare(CLONE_NEWUSER) transiently grants namespace capabilities until dropped
grants.narrowestForm: PR_SET_DUMPABLE(0) and PR_SET_NO_NEW_PRIVS(1) run before namespace creation, capabilities drop immediately, then seccomp installs
grants.whyNoNarrower: Kernel requires user namespace for unprivileged seccomp/capability bounding without root
grants.order: Single-threaded before secret input or worker startup; if dumpable fails, namespace step does not run

grants.grant: secret-protection-core WorkArea and private Rayon worker pool
grants.purpose: Allocate, lock and wipe Argon2id arena and parallel worker stacks
grants.admits: OS RLIMIT_MEMLOCK may decline page locking (is_locked() == false)
grants.narrowestForm: Expose NativeArgon2::is_locked() so callers requiring mlock can refuse before reading secrets
grants.whyNoNarrower: Unprivileged processes cannot override kernel RLIMIT_MEMLOCK
grants.order: Allocate and 64-byte-align WorkArea before spawning workers; wipe worker stacks and arena on every call

grants.admits: Misaligned or mis-sized pointer cast would be undefined behaviour
grants.narrowestForm: Sole unsafe block in crate (unsafe_code = deny); 64-byte alignment enforced in NativeArgon2::new and verified under Miri
grants.whyNoNarrower: argon2::Block exposes no safe zero-copy constructor from &mut [u8]
grants.order: Alignment checked at construction, count computed as area.len() / Block::SIZE, exclusive &mut borrow preserved

grants.purpose: Overwrite 128 KiB of caller and worker stack frames after secret operations
grants.admits: No-op on wasm32 and bounded to 128 KiB on native targets
grants.narrowestForm: Combined with Secret<T> and Zeroizing ownership; target limits documented in SECURITY.md
grants.whyNoNarrower: Safe Rust and WebAssembly provide no portable frame-erasure primitive
grants.order: Runs after inner secret owners drop and across all Rayon worker threads before returning

grants.purpose: Check out repository and spec submodule to run checks and build package
grants.admits: Build scripts and proc-macros execute with read access to repository contents
grants.narrowestForm: persist-credentials: false on checkouts; zero write or OIDC scopes in build/test jobs
grants.order: Checks, fuzzing and packaging finish before attestation or release jobs run

grants.purpose: Sign GitHub build provenance for mhfe-core crate archive
grants.admits: Could attest another artifact if untrusted code executed in the same job
grants.narrowestForm: Dedicated attest job performs no repository checkout and runs no project code
grants.whyNoNarrower: actions/attest-build-provenance requires id-token: write and attestations: write
grants.order: Downloads packaged .crate archive after build/check/fuzz jobs succeed, then signs provenance

grants.purpose: Create draft GitHub release with crate archive and SHA-256 checksum
grants.admits: Token permits repository content/tag writes during that job
grants.narrowestForm: Dedicated release job runs no repository build code and uses SHA-pinned actions
grants.whyNoNarrower: GitHub Actions has no narrower release-only permission scope
grants.order: Runs last after attest job succeeds

findings.title: xtask Cargo manifest version gate skips TOML dependency sub-tables, commented headers, multiline
findings.reproduction: Run CARGO_TARGET_DIR=target/aud-010-harnesses cargo test --locked --manifest-path docs/audits/AUD-010-harnesses/audit-probes/Cargo.toml, which invokes xtask/src/code_rules.rs directly on a synthetic manifest using [dependencies.subtable-wildcard], [dependencies] # comment, and a multiline inline table.
findings.expected: cargo xtask code-rules enforces CORE-25 version-pinning requirements across every valid Cargo TOML dependency syntax.
findings.observed: check_cargo_requirements sets in_dependencies = line.ends_with("dependencies]") without stripping header comments or matching [dependencies.<pkg>] sub-tables, and cargo_dependency inspects single lines only, allowing all three wildcard forms to pass unflagged while catching plain single-line wildcards.
findings.impact: Future manifest edits using TOML dependency sub-tables, commented section headers or multiline inline tables bypass automatic CORE-25 enforcement in CI. All four active manifests at 00c070c currently satisfy CORE-25.
findings.recommendedFix: Strip unquoted # comments before checking TOML section headers, handle or forbid [dependencies.<pkg>] / [dev-dependencies.<pkg>] / [build-dependencies.<pkg>] sub-tables, and join multiline { ... } inline tables before extracting version.
findings.requiredVerification: Add unit tests in xtask/src/code_rules.rs for sub-tables, commented dependency headers and multiline inline tables, then run cargo xtask check.

findings.title: src/repair/code.rs comment still claims stack-only storage and complete wiping on WebAssembly
findings.reproduction: Read src/repair/code.rs:4-9 alongside SECURITY.md:26-29 and reed-solomon-core 0.2.0's Copy type Lanes([u16; MAX_LANES]) passed by value to zip(made).
findings.expected: Module comments and SECURITY.md agree on secret-erasure guarantees and do not claim stronger WebAssembly wiping than pinned dependencies provide (DOC-06, DOC-07).
findings.observed: src/repair/code.rs:4-9 still states unconditionally that every value computed from word numbers is held in fixed arrays on the stack and wiped when it goes out of use on WebAssembly, whereas reed-solomon-core 0.2.0 leaves an unzeroized Lanes copy (AUD-007-SEC002) and wasm32 frame/register placement is compiler-controlled.
findings.impact: Maintainers reading src/repair/code.rs see an overstated internal erasure guarantee that contradicts the repaired text in SECURITY.md.
findings.recommendedFix: Update src/repair/code.rs:4-9 to describe mhfe-core's fixed Zeroizing buffers accurately, note reed-solomon-core 0.2.0's residual unzeroized copy, and reference SECURITY.md for WebAssembly memory behaviour.
findings.requiredVerification: Compare src/repair/code.rs with SECURITY.md and run cargo xtask check.

observations.title: README.md suite 3 wrong-password summary omits the unverified 24-word reading without a count
observations.reproduction: Read README.md:69-72 alongside Recovery::readings(None) in src/mhfe.rs.
observations.expected: Overview prose notes when suite 3 wrong-password detection requires the caller to supply the expected word count.
observations.observed: README.md:69-72 states that for a phrase of 12 to 21 words suite 3 tells a wrong password almost always, without noting there that calling Recovery::readings(None) still yields an unverified 24-word Reading (is_verified() == false).
observations.impact: Informational clarity improvement for callers reading the overview before the API rustdoc.
observations.recommendedFix: Add a brief clause in README.md:69-72 noting that without a stated word count suite 3 also returns an unverified 24-word reading.
observations.requiredVerification: Check wording in README.md against Recovery::readings rustdoc and run dprint check.

limitations: Local AddressSanitizer fuzzing ran 30.99 to 37.99 active seconds per target (1,635,317 total executions, 0 crashes) rather than the 300-second per-target ordinary-audit budget in docs/audits/TARGETS.md.

Miri cannot execute secret-protection-core 0.2.0's libc::sigfillset FFI call, blocking full-crate Miri runs on Secret and WorkArea paths; all 9 syscall-free unit tests and the isolated slice_as_blocks + Argon2id and CyclicWords harness passed under both -Zmiri-strict-provenance and -Zmiri-tree-borrows.
Full-cost Argon2id vector replay (tests/full_cost.rs) was not run locally.
Android (aarch64-linux-android, x86_64-linux-android) and iOS (aarch64-apple-ios, aarch64-apple-ios-sim) were linted and/or cross-linked without emulator or device runtime execution (AUD-006-ARC004).

Two upstream 0.2.0 dependency limitations remain open until their next releases: reed-solomon-core 0.2.0's unzeroized Copy of Lanes (AUD-007-SEC002) and secret-protection-core 0.2.0's abort on NFKD allocation failure (AUD-006-API001).
